summary: Fixes a duplicate assignment of RSVP message type values by changing the values for the Challenge and Integrity Response messages assigned in RFC 2747. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Two kids were given the same locker number. This fixes it by giving two of the messages a new number.

subtitle: Two RSVP Integrity message types get new numbers to end a clash with the Bundle message.

tldr.problem: RFC 2747 gave RSVP Message Type 12 to the Integrity Response message, but RFC 2961 gave the same value to the Bundle message.
tldr.mechanism: This memo changes the Challenge message to Message Type 25 and the Integrity Response message to 25+1, leaving 12 for Bundle.
tldr.outcome: Conformant nodes interoperate using 12 for Bundle and 25 and 26 for the Integrity handshake. Non-conformant ones do not interoperate with them.

today: RFC 3097 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2747. The unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Clash Over Type 12
sections.content:
RFC 2747 (RSVP Cryptographic Authentication) assigns RSVP Message Type 12 to an Integrity Response message. RFC 2961 (RSVP Refresh Overhead Reduction Extensions) assigns the same value to a Bundle message.

The memo resolves this by changing the Integrity Response number. It gives the reasoning: the refresh reduction protocol is believed to have entered use in the field before its publication and before the conflict was noticed, and installing new software may be easier where the Integrity object is deployed than where the refresh reduction extension is.
sections.eli5: Two messages wore the same number tag. The one that fewer people use agrees to change its tag.

sections.title: The Modification
sections.content:
The Message Types defined in the RSVP Integrity extension of RFC 2747 are changed as follows: the Challenge message has Message Type 25, and the Integrity Response message has Message Type 25+1, that is 26.

The Challenge message is renumbered as well, to simplify possible interoperability problems, since the Integrity Response is a reply to it.
sections.eli5: The question and its answer both get new numbers, 25 and 26, so they stay matched as a pair.

sections.title: Compatibility
sections.content:
Two conformant nodes interoperate, using type 12 for Bundle and types 25 and 26 for the Integrity handshake. A non-conformant implementation will not interoperate with a conformant one, although two non-conformant implementations can interoperate as before.

A handshake cannot succeed by accident, because both sides use either the new numbers or the old ones. The Integrity Response also includes a 32-bit cookie that must match the Challenge, or the challenge fails. A non-conformant node should never see a Bundle message as an Integrity Response, because RFC 2961 requires Bundle messages be sent only to Bundle-capable nodes.
sections.eli5: Updated devices understand each other. An old device only works with another old one, and mix-ups are caught by a matching secret number.

references.text: Baker, F., Lindell, R. and M. Talwar, "RSVP Cryptographic Authentication", RFC 2747, January 2000.
Berger, L., Gan, D., Swallow, G., Pan, P., Tommasi, F. and S. Molendini, "RSVP Refresh Overhead Reduction Extensions", RFC 2961, April 2001.
